title: Kernel confidence decay, predictive admission control, and attention autotune regression action plan
creator: Priya Malhotra
description: Summary: Following a scheduler heuristic tweak (canary rollout on 2026-02-20) we saw an unexpected mid-load regression: quantized L2-family models experienced a 15-40% increase in p95 token latency for conversational workloads. Root-cause hypothesis converged on a combination of (a) aggressive kernel candidate pruning that reduced exploration of slightly lower-confidence kernels, and (b) a confidence-decay metric in the kernel selector that underweighted recent successful probes for attention-optimized kernels. The scheduler then pushed more load to slower fallback kernels during sustained bursts. This ticket coordinates follow-ups: fix the confidence decay logic, add a predictive admission control to smooth microbursts, and autotune attention thresholds to avoid over-pruning on quantized paths.
timeline: 2026-02-20: Scheduler heuristic change rolled to 10% canary (internal rollout ID rls-2026-0220-heuristic)
2026-02-21: Observed first p95 increase for quantized L2 models in prod-1 region (~15%)
2026-02-22: Canary expanded to 50%, p95 regressed further to ~35% under moderate concurrency
2026-02-23: Canary paused; engineering on-call started triage and perf decks assembled
2026-02-24: Investigation began — initial signal points to kernel selection scoring drift
2026-03-02: Bench repro created (synthetic chat workload with L2-quant) showing deterministic p95 delta when confidence decay enabled
2026-03-05: Prototype fix for confidence accumulation landed behind feature flag (PR #4682)
2026-03-09: Load-testing with predictive admission control ramped in staging; reduced tail by ~18%
2026-03-12: This action plan documented and owners assigned
investigation_summary: We instrumented kernel selector scores, per-request candidate histories, and scheduler admission events. Two signals were critical: the 'confidence' decay multiplier used when a kernel was probed but not recently selected dropped by 40% due to an off-by-one in the time-bucket aggregation; and the pruning threshold for attention-optimized kernels did not account for quantization-induced timing variance, causing warm candidates to be evicted prematurely. Together these changes reduced the effective candidate pool and elevated the probability the scheduler chose a fallback kernel under burst. Synthetic benchmarks reproduced the effect by toggling the decay factor and pruning thresholds.
decisions: Revert the aggressive pruning heuristic and introduce a softer decay curve: decay multiplier moves from 0.6->0.85 immediate, then linear to 0.5 over 30 minutes
Add a short-term sticky boost for kernels that completed >1 successful probe in the last 10 minutes (sticky window = 10m)
Introduce predictive admission control (PAC) that detects microburst patterns and temporarily raises the candidate pool size during the burst window
Autotune attention pruning thresholds for quantized families using a small continuous calibration job rather than hard static thresholds
Roll fixes behind feature flags and gate rollout by p95 and allocation churn metrics
action_items: ENG-882401-A1: Fix aggregation bug in confidence decay codepath and add unit tests for time-bucket boundaries (owner: Liam)
ENG-882401-A2: Implement sticky-success boost and integrate into kernel scoring pipeline, include metrics to track sticky hits/misses (owner: Serene)
ENG-882401-A3: Build PAC prototype with adjustable detection window and simulated burst tests in staging (owner: Mateo)
ENG-882401-A4: Create autotune calibration job for attention thresholds; schedule as low-priority cron with canary tenants (owner: Anika)
ENG-882401-A5: Extend e2e perf-suite to include quantized L2 chat traces and incorporate in CI perf gate (owner: QA Team)
ENG-882401-A6: Dashboard and alerts: add kernel-pool-size, selector-score-variance, and PAC activation events to runtime console (owner: Observability)
ENG-882401-A7: Run controlled rollback test on canary cluster and validate rollout safety criteria before expanding (owner: SRE)
ENG-882401-A8: Post-deploy 72h monitoring playbook and customer communication template for potentially impacted tenants (owner: Customer Success)
ENG-882401-A9: Write a short postmortem entry linking regression to heuristic AND add this ticket to the stability retro (owner: Priya)
testing_plan: Unit tests for decay math and time-bucket boundaries; microbench harness that replays production candidate histories; staging experiments with synthetic and recorded chat traces; PAC A/B with 5% tenants, measuring p50/p95/p99 and allocation churn; canary expansion only after p95 improvement >=5% and allocation churn within 1.5x baseline for 6 hours.
rollback_and_rollout_plan: All changes gated behind feature flags. Rollout steps: (1) deploy confidence-fix + unit tests to staging, run CI perf gates; (2) enable feature flag for 5% canary tenants in prod-1 for 2 hours of non-peak, monitor p95 and selector metrics; (3) if stable, enable PAC at 5% and monitor for 4 hours; (4) enable sticky boost and autotune calibration for canary tenants; (5) expand canary to 25% then 100% with 24h observation windows. Rollback condition: p95 increases >3% for two consecutive 1h windows or allocation churn >2x baseline. SRE runbook updated with rollback commands and dashboard links.
review_feedback: PM (Arman): prioritize PAC prototype over full autotune if resource-constrained — customers can tolerate a transient calibration period
Design (Maya): make PAC activation visible in Console and add a tooltip explaining why kernels are retained during bursts
SRE (Diego): require explicit traffic shaping test during canary expansion to avoid overloading adjacent clusters
Security (Jin): confirmed no new data plane surface added; autotune job must not log PII — noted
notes: Trade-offs discussed: increasing sticky window and raising candidate pool reduces eviction but can slightly increase average memory pressure and KV cache churn; we will monitor cache eviction metrics and revert tuning if cost delta exceeds threshold

Longer-term idea: incorporate a small reinforcement signal from observed output quality (e.g., hallucination regressions) into kernel scoring to prefer kernels that preserve quality under quantization

This regression highlights brittle coupling between scheduler heuristics and quantization timing variance — propose a follow-on investigation to formalize bounded timing variance tests for new heuristics
closure_criteria: All action items implemented or tracked by follow-up tickets
p95 for quantized L2 chat traces returns to within 2% of pre-regression baseline for 72h after full rollout
No allocation churn or cache-eviction cost increases beyond agreed thresholds
Postmortem summary published and shared with customer-facing teams
